extracted.intended_audience: Snopes readers, fact-check readers, journalists, and anyone interested in Snopes' editorial process
extracted.subtask_description: Snopes' editorial and fact-checking standards describing how items are selected, researched, sourced, reviewed, and corrected for publication on Snopes.com.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to transparency and updates
rubrics_metrics.description: In compliance with the industry principles — and because we think being transparent with readers is the coolest — what follows is a detailed description of our editorial process. We may periodically update this page if and when any aspect of our process changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Snopes declares an ongoing commitment to transparency and to updating its disclosure of process when procedures change; readers are invited to ask questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment and drafting
rubrics_metrics.description: Each entry is assigned to one of the members of our editorial staff who undertakes the preliminary research and writes the first draft of the fact-check.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work is owned by a named staff member who conducts initial research and produces the first draft before additional review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contacting the source of the claim whenever possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Our research begins with (whenever possible) attempting to contact the source of the claim for elaboration and supporting information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attempt to get primary comment or elaboration from the claimant as a first step in research; document contact attempts in the article where made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek expert and documentary sources
rubrics_metrics.description: We also attempt to contact individuals and organizations who would be knowledgeable about, or have relevant expertise in, the subject at hand, as well as searching out printed information (news articles, scientific and medical journal articles, books, interview transcripts, statistical sources) with bearing on the topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine primary outreach with expert interviews and searches of peer-reviewed and other published materials relevant to the claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative research and editorial review
rubrics_metrics.description: Depending upon the nature and complexity of the topic, other members of the editorial staff may contribute additional research (or their own personal expertise) and editing. The final product will pass through the hands of at least one editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complex items may have multiple staff contributors; every piece is edited by at least one editor before publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality gate for publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Any piece that is not deemed up to our standards by one or more editors is subject to further revision and review before being released for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors must be satisfied with a piece's standards; insufficient pieces are revised until they meet editorial standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic selection guided by reader interest, not partisanship
rubrics_metrics.description: We write about whatever items readers are asking about, or searching for, as well as viral rumors that could lead to misunderstandings and purported trivia facts. We don’t choose or exclude items for coverage based on whether they deal with Republican/Democratic, conservative/liberal, or religious/secular issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is demand-driven (searches, reader tips, social trends) and explicitly nonpartisan; politics are a substantial portion of work but not the exclusive focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inputs used to determine reader interest
rubrics_metrics.description: The inputs we use to determine reader interest include the tabulation of terms entered into our search engine, reader email submissions, comments and questions posted to our Twitter and Facebook accounts, what’s trending on Google and social media sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use internal search analytics, reader submissions, social media engagement, and trending topics to prioritize items for investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of formats covered
rubrics_metrics.description: The items we address come in forms that include (but are not limited to) text circulated online, social media posts, image macros/memes, videos, printed material, and articles from other sites and publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fact-checking applies to a wide variety of media formats; reviewers should be prepared to assess images, video, memes, posts, and printed material alike.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions and out-of-scope topics
rubrics_metrics.description: We don’t address, without exception, every single item that comes our way: we may decline to undertake a given topic because it is beyond our scope (e.g., answering the question "Does God exist?") or represents a subject that is not relevant or appropriate for our site (e.g., speculating about a given celebrity’s sexual orientation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decline items that are metaphysical, outside factual verification, irrelevant, or inappropriate to investigate for the site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for non-partisan and authoritative sources
rubrics_metrics.description: We attempt to use non-partisan information and data sources (e.g., peer-reviewed journals, government agency statistics) as much as possible, and to alert readers that information and data from sources such as political advocacy organizations and partisan think tanks should be regarded with skepticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor peer-reviewed literature and government data; flag partisan sources and treat them with caution in analysis and presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources listing and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Any published sources (both paper and digital) that we quote, link to, use as background information for, or otherwise reference in our fact checks are listed in the Sources section at the foot of each fact check article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a Sources section at the article foot listing cited/used published materials; the Sources listing is expandable/collapsible for readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: How direct contacts are noted
rubrics_metrics.description: In cases where we have contacted individuals or organizations by e-mail or telephone for comment, that information is noted within the text of articles and is not usually listed separately in the Sources section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document direct outreach within article prose rather than duplicating it in the Sources list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of embedded media in sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Media embedded within the body of our articles for illustrative or informational purposes, such as YouTube videos and social media posts, are also not separately listed in the Sources section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embedded illustrative media are included inline but not repeated in the Sources list; authors should ensure embedded media are properly attributed within the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections and updates policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Our policy is to promptly correct errors of fact and to clarify any potentially confusing or ambiguous statements in our articles. Readers can submit potential corrections through the Contact form; those submissions will be routed to an editor for evaluation and action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a process for receiving reader-submitted corrections, route them to editors, and act promptly to correct factual errors and clarify ambiguous statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noting substantive changes and rating changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever we change the rating of a fact check (for any reason), correct or modify a substantive supporting fact (even if it does not affect the item’s overall rating), or add substantial new information to an existing article, those changes are noted and explained in an Update box at the foot of the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use an Update box at the article foot to transparently explain any rating changes, substantive fact modifications, or substantial additions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No notation for minor, non-substantive edits
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrections of typographical errors, misspellings, or other minor revisions not deemed substantive by our editors are not noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not clutter the Update history with trivial edits; reserve Update box notes for substantive corrections or rating changes.
